construction_markdown:
No new leaderboard code is submitted. Let `C_*` be the accepted RS–affine `[2^30,1040,535822336]_2` code, let `z_i∈F_2^1040` be its generator columns, and let `j` be its constant-one message, so `j·z_i=1` for every coordinate.

Fix one anchor column `z_*`. For a selector `e∈F_2^n`, form sparse lifted columns `g_i=z_i+e_i z_*`; equivalently, use a singleton when `e_i=0` and an anchored pair when `e_i=1`. The basis-walk compiler from `combinatorial-expander-07` turns these XOR descriptors into valid polynomial-length walks if desired. Append an all-one row to the resulting 1040-row matrix.

The exact row space is `span(C_*,e)`. Consequently this construction has dimension 1041 precisely when `e∉C_*`, and it meets the target precisely when every word in `e+C_*` has weight at least `D`, equivalently every such word has absolute signed sum at most `T=2^21`.

No qualifying selector is supplied. Instead, the proof rules out two broad structured neighborhoods: a successful selector must be at Hamming distance at least 16,384 from every blockwise-affine selector and at least 1,933,312 from every outer-block-independent inner template modulo `C_*`.

For `g_i=z_i+e_i z_*`, appending the constant row gives exactly `span(C_*,e)`: `L_e(j)+1=e`, and then `L_e(x)+(x·z_*)e` recovers every incumbent word. Thus a fixed-anchor sparse lift is precisely the original one-row extension problem, not a new amplification mechanism.

Let `𝒜` be all vectors affine on each `2^15`-coordinate inner block, and let `𝓗={r_h+c:h:F_2^15→F_2, c∈C_*}`, where `r_h` repeats `h` on every outer block. Any target-safe rank-1041 selector must satisfy `dist(e,𝒜)≥16384` and `dist(e,𝓗)≥1933312`. In particular, one nonlinear exceptional block cannot repair an affine selector, and changing at most 58 complete blocks of a repeated template cannot work.

distance_audit: The accepted comparator `C_*` has exact minimum distance `D` and contains `1^n`.

For `e∉C_*`, all new nonzero words are exactly `e+c`, with `c∈C_*`. Because `1^n∈C_*`, their complements occur in the same coset. Hence their lower-distance requirement is equivalent to `|Σ_i(−1)^(e_i+c_i)|≤T` for every `c∈C_*`.
Every blockwise-affine `e_0∉C_*` has a coset word of weight at most `535,805,952=D−16,384` by fixed-inner additive maximality. Perturbing at most 16,383 coordinates cannot restore the target.
For every repeated inner template `r_h`, Parseval supplies an affine inner word at distance at most 16,293 per block. Repeating over 32,768 blocks gives weight at most `533,889,024=D−1,933,312`.
No selector surviving these tests was constructed, so no new minimum distance is claimed.
explicitness_audit: The incumbent field, evaluation set, coordinate order, monomial basis, and affine inner encoder are deterministic and independently audited.
The anchor may be fixed as the first coordinate in the incumbent ordering. Given an explicit selector, every lifted entry is one incumbent entry plus at most one anchored entry.
The obstruction holds for every selector, including noncomputable selectors; it therefore does not rely on random sampling, exhaustive search, conditional expectation, or a hidden lookup.
The parameterized emitter is polynomial-time, but no deterministic selector satisfying the universal coset bound is supplied. Accordingly it is not a leaderboard construction.
The workspace is read-only, so no proof or lemma file was persisted and no validator or dashboard publication run was appropriate.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Parameterized family only. Enumerate the accepted generator rows indexed by `α^r X^s`, `0≤r≤15`, `0≤s≤64`, and coordinates `(a,y)∈A×F_2^15`. Fix the first coordinate `i_*`. Given selector bits `e_i`, emit `L[r,i]=G_*[r,i]⊕(e_i∧G_*[r,i_*])` for all 1040 rows and then emit an all-one row. No selector meeting the target is supplied.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: If a selector bit costs at most `P(log n)` operations and an incumbent entry costs at most `Q(log n)`, emission uses at most `1040Q(log n)+n(P(log n)+1040(Q(log n)+2)+1)` bit operations and outputs exactly `1041n` bits; this is `n^{O(1)}` for polynomial `P,Q`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: Precompute the 1040 anchor entries. For each of the `n` coordinates, compute one selector bit and 1040 incumbent entries, then perform at most one AND and one XOR per row; the last row costs one emitted bit per coordinate. The accepted incumbent entry evaluator is polynomial-time. Thus any explicitly indexed selector yields the complete matrix in polynomial time. Since the missing distance-qualified selector is not provided, this proves only the family emitter's explicitness.

obstructions: The upstream complete Ta-Shma, complete Cartesian, Gray-register, and complete free-walk schedules are already below the incumbent or exceed the length budget.
By the basis-walk compiler, unrestricted sparse-path notation is equivalent to the original explicit balanced-column problem; routing through a good host graph gives no automatic discrepancy control.
The fixed-anchor specialization collapses exactly to adjoining one selector row to `C_*`.
Every selector within 16,383 bits of the full blockwise-affine space fails; in particular, making only one inner block nonlinear is insufficient.
Every selector within 1,933,311 bits of a repeated inner template modulo `C_*` fails; modifications supported on at most 58 whole outer blocks are insufficient.
The theorem does not rule out a genuinely outer-varying nonlinear selector, a variable-anchor schedule, or an unrelated balanced column stream.

proof_markdown:
## Setup

Let `L=2^15`, so the coordinate set is `I=A×Y`, with `|A|=|Y|=L` and `n=L²`. Let `C_*` be the accepted RS–affine code and `G_*` one of its full-rank 1040-row generators. Write its columns as `z_i`. The constant polynomial gives a message `j` satisfying `j·z_i=1` for every `i`.

Fix a column `z_*`. For an arbitrary selector `e∈F_2^I`, define `g_i=z_i+e_i z_*`. For a message `x`, the lifted word is

`L_e(x)_i=x·g_i=(x·z_i)+(x·z_*)e_i`.

### 1. Exact fixed-anchor collapse

Because `j·z_*=1` and the incumbent word of `j` is `1^n`,

`L_e(j)=1^n+e`.

After appending `1^n`, the row space therefore contains `e`. It then contains every incumbent word because

`c_x=L_e(x)+(x·z_*)e`.

Conversely, the displayed formula places every `L_e(x)` in `span(C_*,e)`. Hence

`span(L_e(F_2^1040),1^n)=span(C_*,e)`.

This proves binary linearity and exact length. Since `dim C_*=1040`, the dimension is 1041 exactly when `e∉C_*`; otherwise it remains 1040.

### 2. Exact distance condition

Assume `e∉C_*`. The nonzero words are the old nonzero words of `C_*` and the coset `e+C_*`. The old words already have weight at least `D`. Since `1^n∈C_*`, the complement of every word in `e+C_*` is also in that coset. Thus all new words have weight at least `D` exactly when every new word has weight in `[D,n−D]`, or equivalently

`|Σ_i (−1)^(e_i+c_i)|≤n−2D=T`

for every `c∈C_*`. The anchored path proposal has therefore reduced exactly to finding an admissible one-row extension.

### 3. Robust blockwise-affine obstruction

Let `𝒜=H^A(F^A)` be the space of vectors whose restriction to every outer block is an affine Boolean function of `y`. Each `e_0∈𝒜` has a unique outer symbol vector `v∈F^A`.

If `e_0∉C_*`, the proved fixed-inner additive-maximality lemma applied to `R+<v>` supplies `c∈C_*` such that

`wt(e_0+c)≤535805952=D−16384`.

If `dist(e,e_0)≤16383`, the triangle inequality gives `wt(e+c)≤D−1`, contradicting the target. If instead `e_0∈C_*`, then `e+e_0` itself has weight `dist(e,e_0)` and is a nonzero word of `span(C_*,e)`; the same conclusion follows even more strongly. Therefore every target-safe rank-1041 selector satisfies

`dist(e,𝒜)≥16384`.

As a corollary, one arbitrary nonlinear exceptional block cannot suffice. Indeed, Parseval on one length-`L` block gives an affine approximation within `(L−ceil(sqrt L))/2=(32768−182)/2=16293<16384` positions.

### 4. Robust outer-homogeneous obstruction

For a Boolean function `h:Y→F_2`, let `r_h(a,y)=h(y)`, and define

`𝓗={r_h+c:h:Y→F_2, c∈C_*}`.

Its Walsh coefficients satisfy

`Σ_{ξ∈F_2^15} W_h(ξ)^2=L²`.

There are `L` coefficients, so some has magnitude at least `ceil(sqrt L)=182`. Choosing the affine constant with the favorable sign produces an affine function `b+ξ·y` for which

`wt(h+b+ξ·y)≤(L−182)/2=16293`.

The corresponding affine word repeated on all outer blocks belongs to `C_*`, because it is the encoding of a constant outer polynomial. Hence every coset represented by a member of `𝓗` contains a word of weight at most

`L·16293=533889024=D−59L`.

Changing at most `59L−1=1933311` coordinates still leaves a word below `D`. Thus every target-safe rank-1041 selector obeys

`dist(e,𝓗)≥59L=1933312`.

In particular, a repeated nonlinear template cannot be repaired by changes confined to at most 58 complete outer blocks.

### 5. Scope

The argument is deterministic and information-theoretic. It closes fixed-anchor lifts with blockwise-affine, nearly blockwise-affine, repeated-template, or nearly repeated-template selectors. It does not exclude an arbitrary outer-varying nonlinear selector. By the upstream basis-walk compiler, that remaining case is simply the general problem of constructing a symbolic 1040-dimensional column stream with all nonzero Fourier coefficients bounded by `2^21`.

proof_steps.statement: The exact two-sided signed-sum allowance is `T=2^21`.

proof_steps.proof: For every message `x`, `L_e(x)=c_x+(x·z_*)e`. The constant message gives `L_e(j)=1+e`; after appending one this recovers `e`, and then every `c_x`. The reverse containment follows from the same formula.
proof_steps.statement: The all-one augmentation of the fixed-anchor lift has row space exactly `span(C_*,e)`.

proof_steps.proof: When `e∉C_*`, the only new words are `e+C_*`. Since `1∈C_*`, this coset contains every complement, so minimum weight at least `D` is equivalent to absolute signed sum at most `T` throughout the coset.
proof_steps.statement: A fixed-anchor lift gives a target `[n,1041]` code exactly when its selector is a target-safe one-row extension.

proof_steps.proof: Every non-codeword blockwise-affine representative has a coset word of weight at most `D−16384`; a perturbation of at most 16383 bits remains below `D`. Representatives in `C_*` give the even simpler low word `e+e_0`.
proof_steps.statement: Every successful selector has Hamming distance at least 16,384 from the complete blockwise-affine space.

proof_steps.proof: Parseval gives average squared Walsh coefficient `L`; hence the maximum absolute coefficient is at least `ceil(sqrt L)=182`. Choosing the affine constant flips its sign if necessary.
proof_steps.statement: Every Boolean function on `F_2^15` is within 16,293 positions of some affine function.

proof_steps.proof: Repeat the affine approximation on all `L` outer blocks. The resulting incumbent coset word has weight at most `L·16293=D−59L`; fewer than `59L` further flips cannot reach `D`.
proof_steps.statement: Every successful selector has distance at least `59·2^15=1,933,312` from every repeated inner template modulo `C_*`.

proof_steps.proof: The exact collapse removes fixed-anchor syntax as an independent source of mixing, while the two quantitative lemmas exclude its principal symbolic selector classes. The basis-walk compiler leaves only general outer-varying nonlinear streams or variable-anchor schedules.
proof_steps.statement: No audited fixed-anchor structured selector improves the durable dimension-1040 endpoint; the general sparse column-stream problem remains open.

theorem_statement: Let `C_*` be the accepted RS–affine `[2^30,1040,535822336]_2` code, with generator columns `z_i` and constant message `j`. For any fixed anchor `z_*` and selector `e∈F_2^n`, the lift with columns `g_i=z_i+e_i z_*`, followed by an all-one row, has row space exactly `span(C_*,e)`. It therefore yields dimension 1041 and the target distance if and only if `e∉C_*` and every word of `e+C_*` has absolute signed sum at most `2^21`. Moreover, every such successful selector must be at Hamming distance at least 16,384 from every blockwise-affine selector and at least 1,933,312 from every outer-block-independent inner template modulo `C_*`. Thus fixed-anchor sparse paths provide no shortcut, and their natural affine or repeated-template selector families are rigorously excluded.
title: Fixed-anchor collapse and robust selector obstructions at the k=1041 frontier
